spec: Build a contact-form backend. Visitors submit messages with a name, email and message body; administrators can list all messages and delete individual ones. Messages are stored in DynamoDB.

complexity.rationale: Single message store with create, list, and delete operations.

congruence_checklist: Message model has name, email, body

plan.summary: A JSON REST API that accepts public contact-form submissions (name, email, message body) and stores them in a DynamoDB table, plus an administrator-facing surface to list all stored messages and delete individual ones. Public visitors call the submission endpoint from a website form; administrators call the list/delete endpoints with an API key that the service reads from Secrets Manager. The service runs as a standalone FastAPI process and talks to DynamoDB and Secrets Manager directly with boto3.

endpoints.purpose: Liveness/readiness probe used by the evaluation harness; reports service status and DynamoDB table reachability.
Public contact-form submission. Validates name, email and message body, generates a message id and created_at timestamp, and writes the item to the DynamoDB messages table.
Administrator listing of all stored contact messages via a DynamoDB scan, with optional limit and pagination cursor. Requires the admin API key.
Administrator retrieval of a single message by id (DynamoDB GetItem); returns 404 if it does not exist. Requires the admin API key.
Administrator deletion of a single message by id (DynamoDB DeleteItem); returns 404 if it does not exist. Requires the admin API key.

data_models.name: Message
fields: source_ip: str | None (client IP recorded at submission)

data_models.name: MessageList
fields: next_cursor: str | None (base64 encoded DynamoDB LastEvaluatedKey)

aws_resources.name: contact-form-messages
aws_resources.justification: Primary store required by the spec ('Messages are stored in DynamoDB'). Partition key message_id (S); serves PutItem on submission, Scan for the admin list endpoint, GetItem and DeleteItem for single-message operations. PAY_PER_REQUEST billing.

aws_resources.name: contact-form/admin-api-key
aws_resources.justification: Holds the shared admin API key that the service loads at startup to authorise the administrator list/get/delete endpoints, so the credential is not baked into application configuration.

aws_resources.name: contact-form-backend-app-role
aws_resources.justification: Execution identity assumed by the standalone FastAPI service, with a least-privilege policy granting dynamodb:PutItem/GetItem/DeleteItem/Scan/DescribeTable on the messages table and secretsmanager:GetSecretValue on the admin API key secret, plus CloudWatch logs write access.

aws_resources.name: /contact-form/backend
aws_resources.justification: Log group the application writes structured request and submission/deletion audit logs to, giving administrators operational visibility into the contact form.

assumptions: No Lambda, SQS, SNS or API Gateway is planned: the spec describes only synchronous CRUD over DynamoDB with no asynchronous processing, notification or event-driven workload, and the backend is hosted by the evaluation harness rather than in Lambda.
'Administrators' are authenticated with a single shared API key sent in an X-Api-Key header and validated against the Secrets Manager value; no user accounts or role hierarchy were specified.
Message ids are server-generated UUIDv4 strings; clients never supply an id.

Listing uses a DynamoDB Scan with a default page size of 50 and an opaque cursor, which is acceptable for the low volume expected from a contact form; no secondary index is created because no filtered or sorted query was requested.
Submission is open to unauthenticated visitors, as a public website contact form implies.
Email addresses are validated for format only; no verification email or outbound mail delivery is in scope since the spec does not mention notifications.
Deleting a non-existent message returns 404 rather than silently succeeding.
Timestamps are stored as ISO-8601 UTC strings for readability in the admin listing.

🐍 Generated application code (initial): 5 files — FastAPI contact-form backend split into `app.py` (routes, pydantic models, API-key auth dependency, normalized `{detail, code}` error handlers) and `storage.py` (boto3 DynamoDB repository + Secrets Manager admin-key provider behind small interfaces, plus an in-memory repository and opaque base64 cursor helpers). AWS clients read `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL` and default to us-east-1; table/secret names come from env vars (`contact-form-messages`, `contact-form/admin-api-key`). Email validation uses a stdlib regex validator (no email-validator dependency). Endpoints: GET /health, POST /messages (public), GET/DELETE /messages and /messages/{id} (X-Api-Key protected, 404 on missing). `tests/test_app.py` covers every endpoint, validation failures, pagination, invalid cursor, 401/503 auth paths, and the DynamoDB/Secrets layers using injected fakes via FastAPI dependency overrides — fully offline.

A customer-managed KMS key with rotation and an explicit key policy backs all encryption requirements. Files: versions.tf (terraform block pinning hashicorp/aws ~> 5.0 plus hashicorp/random), variables.tf (defaults matching the plan's resource names), main.tf (provider with project/managed-by default_tags and all resources), outputs.tf. No Lambda, SQS, SNS, API Gateway or unsupported services are created; the only Checkov suppression is CKV2_AWS_57 (secret auto-rotation would require a rotation Lambda outside the plan).
